rationale: I read the complete held EO 12573 (51 FR 40954, signed November 6, 1986, Amending Executive Order No. 11157 as It Relates to Incentive Pay for Hazardous Duty): sec. 1(a) adds a sentence on solid fumigant formulations to subsection (h) of section 109 of Part I of EO 11157, sec. 1(b) adds a new subsection (j) defining handling of chemical munitions, and sec. 2 sets the effective dates (October 1, 1985 for the chemical-munitions amendment; on signature for the pesticide amendment). It is purely an amending order with no independent command and no own term; its text lives only inside EO 11157. I read the held full text of EO 13294 (68 FR 15919, signed March 28, 2003, Regulations Relating to Hazardous Duty Incentive Pay, Aviation Career Incentive Pay, and Submarine Duty Incentive Pay): sec. 2 provides 'Executive Order 11157 of June 22, 1964, as amended, and Executive Order 11800 of August 17, 1974, as amended, are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 11157 'as amended' removes the text EO 12573 inserted, so EO 12573 has no remaining operation. EO 13294 does not name EO 12573 (the ACT record has names_target false), so the end is by revocation of the amended parent. D6 self-check: a search of the held full-run texts for '12573' finds only EO 12573 itself and unrelated page or document-number hits in EO 12673 and EO 9637; no held instrument separately continues, re-enacts or restores the EO 12573 text after 2003. EO 13294 sec. 1 delegates hazardous-duty pay regulation to the Secretaries; any later regulation is their own, not EO 12573. The 1989 snapshot row (amends other document) agrees that its effect merged into EO 11157. Both history observations were reviewed. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing March 28, 2003) is not otherwise adjudicated.
